captureCorpus.sanitizationCaveat: The 2026-08-05 shape-capture round (oidc_claims.json, cosign_keyless_bundle.json, env_protected_one.json, env_protected_list.json) came from a throwaway PUBLIC repository that has since been deleted, with name strings sanitized to OWNER/REPO. The cosign keyless bundle's Fulcio certificate embeds the ORIGINAL repository identity in signed DER, which cannot be string-replaced. Consequence, recorded rather than smoothed over: identity cross-checks between the sanitized JSON and the unsanitized certificate WILL disagree, and the kit reports that disagreement instead of relaxing the check.
captureCorpus.shardingCaveat: Rekor is SHARDED. A REST entry's top-level logIndex is GLOBAL across every shard the log has ever had; verification.inclusionProof.logIndex is LOCAL to the active shard's Merkle tree. On the 2021 capture (logIndex 1000000) the two happen to be equal because that entry predates the shard splits, and an equality check written against that capture alone looked correct. rekor_rest_entry_fresh.json (global 2354787700, shard-local 2232883438) disproves it. The invariant that IS true, and that the kit now enforces when rekor.restLogInfo is supplied, is global - local == sum(inactiveShards[].treeSize) — 121904262 for this capture, exactly.

description: Every output shape this kit is allowed to parse, and the evidence that we have actually seen it. A parser may only succeed on a VALIDATED shape; shapes.ShapeRegistry re-hashes each captureFile at load time and demotes any entry whose capture is missing or altered to BLOCKED. A BLOCKED shape yields AUT_OUTPUT_SHAPE_UNKNOWN no matter how plausible the input looks. Only provenance REAL_CAPTURE may validate a shape, and captures are read ONLY from captures/normalized/ - a hand-authored file under tests_data/ can never be promoted to evidence.

cosign.bundle.keyless.legacy.v1.bindingNote: SHAPE validated, BINDING deliberately not. The capture's JSON was sanitized to OWNER/REPO, but the repository name also lives inside the Fulcio certificate's SIGNED DER, where no sanitiser could reach it: the cert says 'samerzakaria/shipgate-shape-capture'. So cosign.check_certificate_identity() compares the two and DISAGREES on this fixture. That is the correct behaviour of a correct parser meeting a sanitized fixture, and the check is NOT relaxed to make it pass. Fields that were not sanitized still agree: repository_owner_id 228308318, the commit sha c25f0980…, ref, runner environment, event name and OIDC issuer. Binding is proved separately by the synthetic-verifier-result tests in selfcheck.
cosign.bundle.keyless.legacy.v1.note: Captured 2026-08-05 from a THROWAWAY PUBLIC repository, since deleted; the identities are TEST identities. Name strings were sanitized to OWNER/REPO by the capture author. IMPORTANT: this is the LEGACY cosign bundle serialisation {base64Signature, cert, rekorBundle} — a flat triple with no mediaType — NOT a keyless flavour of the sigstore bundle v0.3, which is a different shape and remains BLOCKED under cosign.bundle.keyless.v0_3. The producing cosign version is NOT stated by the capture author, so the version gate cannot be applied to this shape; what is validated is the SHAPE. Real cross-checks that DO hold: base64Signature == the logged signature, cert == the logged public key, and integratedTime 1785949299 falls inside the certificate's 600-second Fulcio validity window [1785949299, 1785949899]. The rekorBundle carries only a SignedEntryTimestamp — there is NO inclusion proof in this shape.

blockedEvidence.says: Generating ephemeral keys... / Non-interactive mode detected, using device flow. — cosign then blocks on a device-code prompt. Evidence of IMPOSSIBILITY, never of a shape: it validates nothing and can never promote this entry.

cosign.bundle.keyless.v0_3.blockedReason: STILL BLOCKED after the 2026-08-06 v0.3 round. bundle_v03.json IS a real sigstore bundle v0.3 — but it is the KEYED variant: verificationMaterial carries publicKey.hint. The keyless variant carries a Fulcio `certificate` instead, which is a different verificationMaterial and a different schema. Capturing the keyed envelope does not validate the keyless one, and marking it VALIDATED from a differently-shaped file is the exact fabrication this registry exists to prevent. The blocker is not tooling: it is that keyless signing needs an OIDC token, and without one cosign falls back to an INTERACTIVE device-code flow and waits for a human at a browser — so no unattended capture is possible in this sandbox. keyless_attempt.txt is that evidence, digest-pinned below and re-hashed at load.
cosign.bundle.keyless.v0_3.note: Parser branch implemented and live: a v0.3 bundle carrying verificationMaterial.certificate or .x509CertificateChain is RECOGNISED as keyless and REFUSED with AUT_OUTPUT_SHAPE_UNKNOWN. Unblock by running `cosign sign-blob --new-bundle-format` keylessly in an environment that HAS an OIDC token (a GitHub Actions job with id-token: write). This does NOT block the keyless identity path, which is live via cosign.bundle.keyless.legacy.v1.

rekor.rest.entry.fresh.v1.bindingNote: SHAPE validated. This is the FIRST proof-carrying REST entry in the corpus that is BOUND to a bundle in the corpus: logIndex 2354787700 and integratedTime 1785990048 both match bundle_v03.json's tlog entry, and the entry's `body` is BYTE-IDENTICAL to that bundle's canonicalizedBody. bindingValidated stays false all the same, and the distinction matters: it binds an entry to a BUNDLE, not a signed identity to a DECISION SUBJECT. The bundle it binds to is KEYED and carries no identity, so this closes the no-fresh-bound-entry gap without closing the identity gap. It is also perishable — integratedTime 1785990048 was ~29 minutes old at registration and ages past the 3600s default window about an hour later, so selfcheck exercises the freshness verifier against a REFERENCE clock (accept at +60s, refuse at +3601s, refuse at -60s) and never against the wall clock, which would make the suite pass today and fail tomorrow.

statusVocabulary.BLOCKED: no real capture exists (or its digest no longer matches); the parser recognises the shape and REFUSES it with AUT_OUTPUT_SHAPE_UNKNOWN
statusVocabulary.VALIDATED: the parse contract was checked against a real capture whose digest is pinned below; the parser may succeed on this shape. Read shapeValidated/bindingValidated: a VALIDATED shape means the SHAPE was seen, NOT that the identity inside it binds to anything
statusVocabulary.bindingValidated: false on every current entry, including the 2026-08-06 round. No capture in this corpus proves a binding between a signed IDENTITY and a real DECISION SUBJECT: the sanitized fixtures deliberately cannot, and the unsanitized ones (both keyed bundles) sign a blob that is not a ship-gate decision and carry no certificate at all. rekor_rest_entry_fresh.json binds an ENTRY to a BUNDLE, which is a real and new binding but not that one. Binding is exercised in selfcheck against a decision built to match the captured digest, and enforced at runtime by cosign.check_binding / cosign.check_certificate_identity.

unblockProcedure: 1. Produce the output in the real environment. 2. Save it byte-exact under captures/raw/ and a UTF-8 copy under captures/normalized/. 3. Add captureFile + captureSha256 here, set status VALIDATED and provenance REAL_CAPTURE. 4. Re-run python3 -m shipgate.authority.selfcheck. Never hand-author a capture.

versionTiers.NOT-CAPTURED: The shape is BLOCKED and no output of it exists, so there is no producing version to state. Also not UNSTATED: there is no capture whose provenance could have been omitted.
versionTiers.OBSERVED-CAPTURE: The producing tool printed its own version and that output is IN the corpus. Strongest tier. cosign v3.1.3 (cosign_version_3_1_3.json) for the 2026-08-06 v0.3 round; cosign v3.1.2 (cosign_version.json) for the original round.
versionTiers.OPERATOR-ASSERTED-CONFIRMED: No `--version` capture exists for this tool, but the operator stated the version and the capture author has since confirmed it. cosign v3.1.2 and rekor-cli v1.5.3 for the original cosign/rekor corpus; gh 2.65.0 for the gh repo/environment/secrets captures. The gh entries additionally carry `versionCorroboration`, a link to the upstream release record (cli/cli tag v2.65.0, published 2025-01-06), so the version and its date are checkable against something outside this repository. That is corroboration of the CLAIM, not observation of the producing binary, which is why it does not promote the tier to OBSERVED-CAPTURE. The gate MAY apply the range; what is VALIDATED is still the shape.
versionTiers.RUNNER-RESOLVED: We know EXACTLY how the tool was installed, and that mechanism does not pin a version. The three trust-shape captures came from a GitHub Actions job in a throwaway public repository, since deleted: cosign was installed by sigstore/cosign-installer@v3, which resolves to whatever the latest v3.x was at job time, and gh was the runner's ambient install. RUNNER-RESOLVED IS NOT UNSTATED. "we know the install mechanism and it does not pin" is a different — and better — epistemic state than "nobody told us". The version constraint is null: inventing a plausible number to make this column look uniform is precisely the fabrication this registry exists to prevent.
versionTiers.SERVER-API: There is no client tool to version. The Rekor REST shapes are documents returned by rekor.sigstore.dev over api/v1; what is pinned is the API version and the capture digest. Not a tool-version claim at all, so no range applies.
versionTiers.UNSTATED: RETIRED as of 2026-08-06. It formerly covered cosign.bundle.keyless.legacy.v1 and gh.environment.protected.v1; both are now RUNNER-RESOLVED, which says the same 'no version gate applies' with the reason attached. No entry in this manifest uses UNSTATED, and selfcheck asserts that.
versionTiers.purpose: Every shape names the tool version that produced ITS capture, and the EPISTEMIC STATE of that claim. There are four distinct situations in this corpus, not one, and flattening them into a single column would be a lie of uniformity. `versionTier` is the state; `versionConstraint` is the range the gate may enforce, and it is null wherever no version can honestly be pinned.
